rationale: Both passages narrate an angel announcing a virginal conception of Jesus by the Holy Spirit, to the two people closest to the event, with one instruction worded identically in English translation: "you are to give Him the name Jesus" (Matthew 1:21, BSB) and "you are to give Him the name Jesus" (Luke 1:31, BSB). The label is "strong" rather than "explicit" because neither text cites, names, or quotes the other -- the two accounts differ in who receives the message (Joseph vs. Mary), setting, and most of their content (Luke includes the Davidic-throne promise and an extended dialogue; Matthew anchors in the Isaiah 7:14 formula quotation), so the connection rests on the shared event and the matching wording, not on either Gospel pointing to the other.
